title: Why you procrastinate even when it feels bad

blocks.en_text: It’s 5 p.m. and you’ve just realized that report you’ve been putting off
blocks.zh_text: 现在是下午5点，你刚意识到那份一直拖着没做的报告

blocks.en_text: is due tomorrow.
blocks.zh_text: 明天就要交了。

blocks.en_text: It’s time to buckle down, open your computer...
blocks.zh_text: 该埋头干活了，打开电脑……

blocks.en_text: and check your phone.
blocks.zh_text: 然后刷起了手机。

blocks.en_text: Maybe catch up on your favorite YouTube channel?
blocks.zh_text: 要不先看看你最喜欢的YouTube频道？

blocks.en_text: Actually, you should probably make dinner first.
blocks.zh_text: 其实，你可能应该先做晚饭。

blocks.en_text: You usually like cooking,
blocks.zh_text: 你平时挺喜欢做饭的，

blocks.en_text: though it’s hard to enjoy with this work hanging over your head,
blocks.zh_text: 可这活儿压在心头，实在很难享受，

blocks.en_text: and oh— it’s actually pretty late!
blocks.zh_text: 哎呀——其实已经挺晚了！

blocks.en_text: Maybe you should just try again in the morning?
blocks.zh_text: 要不还是明天早上再试试吧？

blocks.en_text: This is the cycle of procrastination, and I promise you, we have all been there.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是拖延的循环，我向你保证，我们都经历过。

blocks.en_text: But why do we keep procrastinating even when we know it’s bad for us?
blocks.zh_text: 可为什么明知拖延对我们不好，我们还是一直拖呢？

blocks.en_text: To be clear, putting something off isn’t always procrastinating.
blocks.zh_text: 先说清楚，把事情往后推并不一定就是拖延。

blocks.en_text: Responsible time management requires deciding which tasks are important
blocks.zh_text: 负责任的时间管理需要判断哪些任务重要

blocks.en_text: and which ones can wait.
blocks.zh_text: 哪些可以往后放。

blocks.en_text: Procrastination is when we avoid a task we said we would do, for no good reason,
blocks.zh_text: 拖延是指我们毫无正当理由地逃避自己说过要做的事，

blocks.en_text: despite expecting our behavior to bring negative consequences.
blocks.zh_text: 尽管我们预料到这种行为会带来负面后果。

blocks.en_text: Obviously, it’s irrational to do something you expect to harm you.
blocks.zh_text: 显然，做一件你预料会伤害自己的事是不理性的。

blocks.en_text: But ironically, procrastination is the result of our bodies trying to protect us,
blocks.zh_text: 但讽刺的是，拖延其实是我们的身体在试图保护我们，

blocks.en_text: specifically by avoiding a task we see as threatening.
blocks.zh_text: 具体来说，就是避开一项我们视为威胁的任务。

blocks.en_text: When you realize you need to write that report,
blocks.zh_text: 当你意识到自己得写那份报告时，

blocks.en_text: your brain responds like it would to any incoming threat.
blocks.zh_text: 你的大脑的反应就像面对任何即将到来的威胁一样。

blocks.en_text: Your amygdala, a set of neurons involved in emotional processing
blocks.zh_text: 你的杏仁核——一组参与情绪处理

blocks.en_text: and threat identification,
blocks.zh_text: 和威胁识别的神经元——

blocks.en_text: releases hormones including adrenaline that kick off a fear response.
blocks.zh_text: 会释放包括肾上腺素在内的激素，启动恐惧反应。

blocks.en_text: This stress-induced panic can overpower the impulses from your prefrontal cortex,
blocks.zh_text: 这种压力引发的恐慌会压过前额叶皮层发出的冲动，

blocks.en_text: which typically help you think long term and regulate your emotions.
blocks.zh_text: 而前额叶皮层通常帮你做长远思考、调节情绪。

blocks.en_text: And it’s in the midst of this fight, flight, or freeze response
blocks.zh_text: 正是在这种战斗、逃跑或僵住反应之中，

blocks.en_text: that you decide to handle the threat
blocks.zh_text: 你决定这样应对威胁：

blocks.en_text: by avoiding it in favor of some less stressful task.
blocks.zh_text: 避开它，转而去做一些压力更小的任务。

blocks.en_text: This response might seem extreme—
blocks.zh_text: 这种反应看起来可能有点极端——

blocks.en_text: after all, it’s just a deadline, not a bear attack.
blocks.zh_text: 毕竟，这只是个截止日期，又不是熊袭击。

blocks.en_text: But we’re most likely to procrastinate tasks that evoke negative feelings,
blocks.zh_text: 但我们最容易拖延的，往往是那些引发负面情绪的任务，

blocks.en_text: such as dread, incompetence, and insecurity.
blocks.zh_text: 比如恐惧、无能感和不安全感。

blocks.en_text: Studies of procrastinating university students have found participants
blocks.zh_text: 对拖延的大学生进行的研究发现，参与者

blocks.en_text: were more likely to put off tasks they perceived as stressful or challenging.
blocks.zh_text: 更容易推迟那些他们认为有压力或有挑战性的任务。

blocks.en_text: And the perception of how difficult the task is
blocks.zh_text: 而对任务难度的感知

blocks.en_text: increases while you’re putting it off.
blocks.zh_text: 会在你拖延的过程中不断加剧。

blocks.en_text: In one experiment, students were given reminders to study throughout the day.
blocks.zh_text: 在一项实验中，学生们全天都会收到学习的提醒。

blocks.en_text: While they were studying, most reported that it wasn’t so bad.
blocks.zh_text: 在学习的时候，大多数人表示其实没那么糟。

blocks.en_text: But when they were procrastinating,
blocks.zh_text: 但当他们在拖延时，

blocks.en_text: they consistently rated the idea of studying as very stressful,
blocks.zh_text: 他们一直把学习这件事评价为压力很大，

blocks.en_text: making it difficult to get started.
blocks.zh_text: 导致很难开始动手。

blocks.en_text: Because procrastination is motivated by our negative feelings,
blocks.zh_text: 因为拖延是由我们的负面情绪驱动的，

blocks.en_text: some individuals are more susceptible to it than others.
blocks.zh_text: 所以有些人比其他人更容易拖延。

blocks.en_text: People who have difficulty regulating their emotions
blocks.zh_text: 那些难以调节自己情绪的人

blocks.en_text: and those who struggle with low self-esteem
blocks.zh_text: 以及那些自尊心较低、为此挣扎的人

blocks.en_text: are much more likely to procrastinate,
blocks.zh_text: 拖延的可能性要大得多，

blocks.en_text: regardless of how good they are at time management.
blocks.zh_text: 不管他们有多擅长时间管理。

blocks.en_text: However, it's a common misconception that all procrastinators are lazy.
blocks.zh_text: 然而，一个常见的误解是，所有拖延的人都很懒。

blocks.en_text: In the body and brain, laziness is marked by no energy and general apathy.
blocks.zh_text: 在身体和大脑层面，懒惰的特征是没有精力、普遍冷漠。

blocks.en_text: When you’re feeling lazy, you’re more likely to sit around doing nothing
blocks.zh_text: 当你感到懒散时，你更可能坐着什么都不做，

blocks.en_text: than distract yourself with unimportant tasks.
blocks.zh_text: 而不是用无关紧要的事情来分散自己的注意力。

blocks.en_text: In fact, many people procrastinate because they care too much.
blocks.zh_text: 事实上，很多人拖延是因为他们太在乎了。

blocks.en_text: Procrastinators often report a high fear of failure,
blocks.zh_text: 拖延者常常表示自己非常害怕失败，

blocks.en_text: putting things off because they’re afraid their work
blocks.zh_text: 把事情往后推，是因为他们害怕自己的成果

blocks.en_text: won’t live up to their high standards.
blocks.zh_text: 达不到自己的高标准。

blocks.en_text: Whatever the reason for procrastination, the results are often the same.
blocks.zh_text: 不管拖延的原因是什么，结果往往都是一样的。

blocks.en_text: Frequent procrastinators are likely to suffer from anxiety and depression,
blocks.zh_text: 经常拖延的人很可能饱受焦虑和抑郁之苦，

blocks.en_text: ongoing feelings of shame,
blocks.zh_text: 持续感到羞耻，

blocks.en_text: higher stress levels and physical ailments associated with high stress.
blocks.zh_text: 压力水平更高，还会出现与高压相关的身体不适。

blocks.en_text: Worst of all, while procrastination hurts us in the long run,
blocks.zh_text: 最糟糕的是，虽然拖延从长远来看会伤害我们，

blocks.en_text: it does temporarily reduce our stress level,
blocks.zh_text: 但它确实会暂时降低我们的压力水平，

blocks.en_text: reinforcing it as a bodily response for coping with stressful tasks.
blocks.zh_text: 从而强化它作为一种应对压力任务的身体反应。

blocks.en_text: So, how can we break the cycle of procrastination?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，我们怎样才能打破拖延的循环呢？

blocks.en_text: Traditionally, people thought procrastinators needed to cultivate
blocks.zh_text: 传统上，人们认为拖延者需要培养

blocks.en_text: discipline and practice strict time management.
blocks.zh_text: 自律，并练习严格的时间管理。

blocks.en_text: But today, many researchers feel the exact opposite.
blocks.zh_text: 但如今，许多研究者的看法恰恰相反。

blocks.en_text: Being too hard on yourself can layer additional bad emotions onto a task,
blocks.zh_text: 对自己太苛刻，会给一项任务叠加更多糟糕的情绪，

blocks.en_text: making the threat even more intense.
blocks.zh_text: 让这种威胁感变得更加强烈。

blocks.en_text: To short-circuit this stress response,
blocks.zh_text: 为了短路这种压力反应，

blocks.en_text: we need to address and reduce these negative emotions.
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要处理并减少这些负面情绪。

blocks.en_text: Some simple strategies include breaking a task into smaller elements
blocks.zh_text: 一些简单的策略包括把一项任务拆成更小的部分，

blocks.en_text: or journaling about why it's stressing you out
blocks.zh_text: 或者写日记，记录它为什么让你感到压力，

blocks.en_text: and addressing those underlying concerns.
blocks.zh_text: 并处理这些潜在的担忧。

blocks.en_text: Try removing nearby distractions that make it easy to impulsively procrastinate.
blocks.zh_text: 试着移除身边那些让你容易冲动拖延的干扰物。

blocks.en_text: And more than anything, it helps to cultivate an attitude of self-compassion,
blocks.zh_text: 最重要的是，培养自我同情的态度会很有帮助，

blocks.en_text: forgiving yourself, and making a plan to do better next time.
blocks.zh_text: 原谅自己，并制定一个下次做得更好的计划。

blocks.en_text: Because a culture that perpetuates this cycle of stress and procrastination
blocks.zh_text: 因为一种让这种压力和拖延的循环持续下去的文化，

blocks.en_text: hurts all of us in the long term.
blocks.zh_text: 从长远来看会伤害我们所有人。
